verdicts.claim: By default every connection runs an automatic checkpoint after any COMMIT that leaves the WAL at 1000 pages or more ... always PASSIVE
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages' and 'checkpoints ... by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE'

verdicts.claim: SQLite 3.51.0 (2025-11-04) added PRAGMA wal_checkpoint=NOOP and the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP mode for sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2()
verdicts.evidence: changes.html 2025-11-04 (3.51.0) section: 'Add the PRAGMA wal_checkpoint=NOOP; command and the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP argument for sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2()'

verdicts.claim: The WAL-reset bug is likely present in SQLite 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09). It is fixed in 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) ... backports 3.44.6 and 3.50.7
verdicts.evidence: wal.html §11: 'likely present in all version of SQLite from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09). It is fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) and later. Backports ... 3.44.6 and 3.50.7'

verdicts.claim: SQLite withdrew 3.52.0 (2026-03-06) and moved its features to 3.53.0. The newest release on 2026-10-16 is 3.54.1
verdicts.evidence: changes.html: '2026-03-06 (3.52.0) Withdrawn ... features ... moved forward into version 3.53.0'; top entry '2026-10-16 (3.54.1)'

verdicts.claim: Litestream v0.5.x runs PASSIVE checkpoints at min-checkpoint-page-count (default 1000) and every checkpoint-interval (default 1m). At truncate-page-n (default 121359 pages, ~500 MB) it tries PASSIVE before TRUNCATE
verdicts.evidence: Guide: 'truncate-page-n: 121359 # Default: ~500MB', 'Attempts a PASSIVE checkpoint first, then falls back to a TRUNCATE', 'min-checkpoint-page-count: 1000', 'checkpoint-interval: 1m'

verdicts.claim: In v10, if readers block that checkpoint beyond the default 250 ms wait, the snapshot aborts and retries a few seconds later
verdicts.evidence: O'Toole: 'waiting up to 250ms by default' and 'v10 ... Either snapshots are fast, or they are aborted, to be retried a few seconds later'

verdicts.claim: Phil Eaton reproduced the WAL-reset bug ... 1 GiB mmap_size ... Against 3.51.2 lost a committed transaction within about 4 seconds; 3.53.0 lost none over ~16 s
verdicts.evidence: Eaton: 'PRAGMA mmap_size=1073741824'; walrace-present 'permanently lost: 1 transactions ... real 0m3.454s'; walrace-absent 'permanently lost: 0 transactions ... real 0m15.946s'

verdicts.claim: In a 2021 SQLite Forum case with 36 connections and about 1000 writes per second, setting PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=0 on every connection made RESTART succeed
verdicts.evidence: Forum: '36 connections open from the same process, about 1000 writes per second' and 'Setting PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=0; on every connection ... lets PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(RESTART); succeed reliably'

verdicts.claim: A prepared statement never reset or finalized can keep a transaction open ... Richard Hipp gave this diagnosis in 2021 for a user whose WAL had grown to about 100 GB
verdicts.evidence: Forum: 'the WAL-File is about 100GB'; 'By Richard Hipp (drh) on 2021-04-06': transaction closes when last prepared statement is reset or finalized

verdicts.claim: Tailscale took manual control of checkpointing ... Starting in August 2025 repeated corruption ~six months ... Dan found and fixed on 2026-03-03
verdicts.evidence: Register: 'in August 2025 those backups began detecting database corruption, repeatedly', 'six months of hunting', 'we take manual control of the checkpoint process'; wal.html: 'On 2026-03-03, one of the SQLite developers (Dan) found and fixed'

notes: All 10 claims verified from the local source cache; 0 web fetches used.
No reviewer-addressed or instruction-like text was found in the cached source excerpts read.
The draft's Litestream-vs-SQLite PASSIVE SQLITE_BUSY disagreement is accurately quoted: the Litestream guide says PASSIVE 'returns SQLITE_BUSY if readers or writers are active'.
